comparator.name: Economics and Business Economics
comparator.sourceNotes: The current student curriculum explicitly establishes a 180-EC, three-year programme: 135 EC in the major when no dedicated minor is selected, 45 EC of optional-course-profile space and a 15-EC bachelor thesis. This reconstruction follows the no-dedicated-minor structure, preserves all 45 EC of genuine open profile space and instantiates each restricted choice neutrally from the current official display order. The four named study routes are flexible groupings that may be combined rather than mutually exclusive formal specialisations; the first-listed Economics direction supplies the three year-three major electives without storing a formal route.

alternatives.label: Economics, business and data
alternatives.labelReason: The completed UCR curriculum is broader than pure economics: it combines micro- and macroeconomics with accounting, finance, marketing, strategy, organisational study, data science, econometrics and international business.
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible response combining micro- and macroeconomics with public economics, accounting, finance, strategy, organisations, marketing, statistics, data and econometrics.
progression: Business, economics, data, research, mathematical and strategic foundations precede the advanced policy, organisational, international-business, machine-learning, econometrics, behavioural-economics, market-research and finance work. Strategy follows Business Foundations; Probability & Statistics follows Mathematical Methods; Money, Banking & Finance follows business, accounting and economic study. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.
traceOverrides: provides multivariate statistics and experimental methods that strengthen empirical economic and business research

alternatives.label: Public economics, institutions and inequality
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum makes public economics, political institutions, law, inequality and policy research its organising emphasis while retaining economics and quantitative foundations.
alternatives.concept: An economics-and-public-policy direction combining markets, macroeconomics and econometrics with political institutions, law, inequality, governance, social theory and policy research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces accounting, marketing, business strategy, international business, product design, machine learning, probability and finance with comparative politics, sociology, qualitative methods, political philosophy, human rights, constitutional law, sustainability governance, EU politics, social theory, persuasive communication, peace and conflict, and historical research. The resulting curriculum is organised around institutions and policy rather than firms and business functions.
progression: Foundational economics, politics and sociology precede advanced public economics, governance, constitutional law, EU politics, social theory, policy communication and research. Qualitative Research Methodology precedes the final research seminar; Research Methods & Statistics precedes econometrics. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

alternatives.label: Finance, economics and quantitative analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around finance and economics with substantial mathematics, programming, data, econometrics and optimisation, rather than implying a specialist finance degree without a quantitative core.
alternatives.concept: A financial-economics direction combining money, banking and corporate finance with micro- and macroeconomics, public economics, econometrics, probability, calculus, programming, databases, machine learning and optimisation.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces experimental methods, marketing, consumer-product work, organisational psychology and market research with programming, database systems, computational decision-making, linear algebra and advanced calculus. It therefore retains the economics and business core while making quantitative financial and economic analysis the organising emphasis. It differs still more clearly from the behavioural route, which concentrates on psychology, marketing, persuasion and consumer response.
progression: Business Foundations precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation and Money, Banking & Finance. Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics, Linear Algebra and Advanced Calculus; programming precedes computational decision-making; accounting, economics, data and research foundations precede the final finance, econometrics and behavioural-economics work. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match covers the programme-wide economics, business and empirical core. Direct interests and the official flexible study routes support two further coherent directions: public economics with institutions and inequality, and finance with quantitative analysis. Both produce feasible curricula that are substantively distinct from the closest match and from each other. Management and innovation also remain supportable, but production stops at the maximum of three alternatives.

blocks: UCR Introduction to Economics covers the programme-wide economic foundations contained in the comparator introduction.
The comparator has a separate compulsory introductory microeconomics course; UCR Introduction to Economics is already shown at its own full credit weight rather than duplicated.
The comparator requires a dedicated intermediate macroeconomics course; UCR International Macroeconomics is shown at its own 7.5-EC scope.
Both introduce firms, markets, strategy and organisational decision-making.
UCR combines statistics with broader research design.
Both examine institutions and policy responses to market and societal problems; the UCR course focuses sustainability governance.
Both examine inequality and institutional outcomes, with different disciplinary emphases.
Both provide reflective context for economic judgment, but the comparator course is specifically historical.
The comparator requires a 15-EC applied research course and bachelor thesis. UCR optional independent research is displayed alongside it as a comparison-only element.

notes.text: Utrecht provides a fixed economics-and-business core, 45 EC of genuine optional-profile space, flexible thematic study routes and a compulsory 15-EC applied-economics thesis. UCR can build coherent economics/business/data, public-economics/institutions and finance/quantitative pathways, but it does not reproduce the same specialist sequence or compulsory economics thesis.
